# v1.1.0-dev.54 — Monitor remap fixed end to end, plus 67 reviewed defects

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.53`.

Two independent review passes over the whole codebase (one on the
dev.53 changes, one on every subsystem) produced 37 verified
high/medium defects and ~30 low-severity ones. **All of them are fixed
in this release.** Every claim was traced against the code before being
accepted; one was refuted and dropped.

## Fixed — monitor remap (the headline)

Remapping a profile onto a different monitor arrangement was unreliable
in three compounding ways, all fixed:

- **Targets could land on the wrong monitor.** A remap target names a
  *current* monitor, but geometry resolved it through the saved monitor
  that happened to share the same role name — so whenever roles had
  shuffled since the save (exactly when you need a remap), crossed
  remaps could invert.
- **Hold undid your remap within a tick.** The 350 ms enforcement poller
  had no idea a remap had been applied; it read the profile's on-disk
  roles, decided every remapped window was in the wrong place, and put
  them all back. Hold now enforces the remapped layout, and forgets it
  when the hold is released or a plain load runs.
- **Monitor pairings could resolve to the wrong role.** The
  index-to-role translation assumed the monitor binding lined up with
  the save-time monitor snapshot — which isn't guaranteed, since you can
  bind on a different setup than you saved on, and Update replaces the
  snapshot. Pairings now resolve by monitor geometry.

Auto-activation also now pairs against the monitor set that actually won
its ranking (a *learned* set can outrank the primary binding) and
re-applies that set's learned remap instead of re-guessing.

## Fixed — restore reliability

- **Re-assert retries could steal a window that was already placed.** A
  retry now knows which windows earlier passes claimed.
- **A cancelled retry chain could come back to life.** Loads are
  serialized and carry a generation token, so a chain suspended mid-await
  can no longer resurrect on top of a newer load, and two loads can no
  longer interleave.
- Only the virtual-desktop moves that actually failed get retried —
  previously one failure re-queued all of them, re-applying geometry over
  windows you'd since moved by hand.
- `--load=work` no longer silently releases Hold on `Work` (profile names
  resolve case-insensitively on Windows).
- Windows half-dragged past a screen edge are captured instead of
  silently dropped.
- Blacklist rules written as `chrome.exe` now match (Task Manager's
  spelling); blacklisted windows no longer create false ambiguity that
  quietly disabled Hold enforcement.

## Fixed — updater

- A malformed sha256 in the update feed now **invalidates the update**
  rather than silently skipping verification — it's the only integrity
  check on an unsigned build.
- The update helper survives non-ASCII user paths (a username like
  `José` previously meant the app quit and never came back), detects a
  failed hand-off instead of exiting anyway, and falls back to a direct
  launch on machines where Windows Script Host is disabled by policy.
- The update dialog's "View" button works again (it pointed at
  dougfessler.com while the allow-list still only permitted github.com).
- Feed redirects are followed correctly, so a hosting change can't
  silently strand every future update check.

## Fixed — your data

- Saving over a **corrupt** profile now preserves the damaged file
  instead of overwriting it, and restoring an old version works even
  when the current file is the broken one — which is precisely when you
  need it.
- **Update no longer wipes each window's revert history.**
- A failed pre-Update snapshot now warns instead of silently leaving the
  Update un-undoable.
- Restoring an old version can no longer resurrect a stale "live" flag
  and leave two profiles marked as held.
- Confirming an overwrite for a name differing only in capitalization now
  works instead of erroring out.
- One hand-edited profile with a malformed name no longer takes down the
  entire profile list.
- All settings/profile/blacklist writes now flush to disk before the
  atomic rename — the crash-safety the code claimed, now true for power
  loss too.

## Fixed — interface

- Unsaved edits survive every profile-switch path (vim keys, quick
  filter, command palette); a failed save keeps the unsaved marker or
  retries instead of dropping your work; switching away and back during
  a save no longer resurrects the pre-save state.
- Escape closes the modal you're actually looking at; Escape in the
  hotkey capture no longer closes all of Settings; Tab works inside
  dialogs instead of trapping focus on the default button; Enter on a
  focused button no longer fires two actions at once.
- Finishing a drag no longer silently moves the selection to a window
  underneath, and Delete/undo are inert mid-drag.
- The window count stays correct after undo/redo; the profile filter
  survives list refreshes; the command palette stops fighting arrow keys.
- Virtual-desktop support on early Windows 11 builds (21H2 / early 22H2)
  now uses the interface identifiers those builds actually expose — the
  fallback path advertised in dev.53 could never have worked.
- Close-to-tray explains itself once instead of on every close; a
  notification suppressed by full-screen or quiet hours no longer eats
  the next one; Hold's border shows at startup; new profiles appear in
  the tray menu and jump list immediately.

## Tests

13 suites, 240+ assertions, all green — including a new persistence-guard
suite covering corrupt-file preservation, revert-history retention, and
the live-flag invariant.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53. Otherwise unzip and run.
